description: Where Ambition Meets Innovation At LPL’s Global Capability Center, you'll find a collaborative culture where your voice matters, integrity guides every decision, and technology fuels progress. Job Overview: We are looking for a UI Automation Test Engineer II who is passionate about quality, automation, and delivering exceptional user experiences. In this role, you will design and maintain UI test automation frameworks, drive end-to-end test coverage for web applications, and partner closely with development and product teams to ship reliable, high-quality software. Responsibilities: Design, develop, and maintain automated UI test suites for web applications and API using frameworks such as Playwright, Selenium, Cypress. Write clear, reusable, and maintainable test code using JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python. Develop end-to-end, integration, and regression test coverage aligned to acceptance criteria and user stories. Execute automated test runs locally and within CI/CD pipelines; triage and report failures promptly. Collaborate with developers, designers, and product managers to identify testable requirements early in the development lifecycle. Participate in sprint ceremonies, contribute to test planning, and provide quality sign-off for feature releases. Identify, document, and communicate defects with clear reproduction steps; track issues through to resolution. Review pull requests for testability and contribute to test code quality standards. Continuously evaluate and improve test automation coverage, execution speed, and reliability. Contribute to test strategy documentation and quality best practices across the engineering team. Design, build, and maintain scalable automated test frameworks for functional, regression, integration, and end-to-end testing. Develop and execute automated test suites for data pipelines, APIs, and cloud-based applications on AWS. Validate data accuracy, completeness, and integrity across ETL/ELT workflows, data warehouses, and data platforms. Leverage AI and ML tools to enhance test coverage, generate test cases, and improve anomaly detection. Collaborate with Engineering, Data, and Product teams to define quality standards, acceptance criteria, and test strategies. Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines and monitor test results across deployment stages. Identify, document, and track defects; drive root cause analysis and work with development teams toward resolution. Contribute to quality documentation, test plans, and best practices across the engineering organization. Participate in code reviews for test code and provide feedback on testability of application designs. What are we looking for? The ideal candidate has hands-on experience with modern UI automation tools, a solid understanding of frontend application behavior, and the discipline to build maintainable, scalable test suites that integrate seamlessly into CI/CD pipelines. Requirements: 5+ years of experience in software quality engineering with a focus on UI automation. Hands-on proficiency with one or more UI automation frameworks such as Playwright, Selenium, Cypress Strong working knowledge of JavaScript or TypeScript; Python experience is a plus. Experience writing page object model (POM) or similar structured test architectures. Solid understanding of web technologies including HTML, CSS, DOM, and browser developer tools. Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD pipelines using tools such as GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or Azure DevOps. Ability to analyze test failures, debug issues, and distinguish test flakiness from genuine defects. Experience with API testing to complement UI coverage (Postman or similar). Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively across engineering and non-engineering stakeholders. Preferences: Experience testing Angular, single-page applications. Familiarity with accessibility testing tools and standards (WCAG, axe-core, Lighthouse). Exposure to visual regression testing tools such as Percy or Applitools. Experience with cross-browser and mobile testing strategies. Knowledge of BDD frameworks such as Cucumber or SpecFlow. Familiarity with test reporting tools such as Allure, TestRail, or similar. AWS or cloud platform experience is a plus. Core Competencies: Excellent verbal and written communication skills Strong analytical and problem-solving skills Ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams Strong ownership mindset and attention to detail Experience working in Agile environments Commitment to continuous learning LPL Global Business Services, LLP - PRIVACY POLICY

title: Senior Engineer-Test Automation
description: Why Ryan? Translate business and technical requirements into meaningful manual and automated test cases. Define and evolve the overall automation strategy aligned with enterprise standards and release cadence. Estimate, prioritize, and plan testing activities in collaboration with Product and Engineering leads. Automation Framework Development Design, implement, and maintain scalable automation frameworks. Integrate tests into continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines and ensure fast feedback. Work closely with DevOps to optimize pipeline execution, parallelization of test execution, and environment provisioning. Drive root-cause analysis sessions for escaped defects and champion preventive actions. Maintain meticulous documentation for all testing activities to ensure auditability and knowledge retention. Collaboration and Execution Partner with application developers to troubleshoot issues and document defects. Work closely with product managers, user experience (UX) designers, and business stakeholders. Contribute to project planning and estimation for features and enhancements. Own and improve user interface (UI), application programming interface (API), and database automation frameworks to increase coverage and accelerate release cycles. Solution Ownership: End-to-end accountability for test coverage, environment stability, and release certification. Collaboration and Influence: Clear, concise communication and the ability to advocate for quality in technical forums and executive updates. Execution Excellence: Consistently delivers reliable, maintainable test suites under tight timelines. Continuous Improvement: Proactively introduces tooling, process enhancements, and emerging best practices. What You Bring Six to nine years of experience in software quality engineering with a focus on automation for web and API-based applications. Proficiency in C#/.NET Core, test frameworks such as Selenium, Playwright, and SpecFlow, and API testing tools such as Postman and JMeter. Hands-on experience with CI/CD and Azure or AWS cloud services. Strong SQL skills and experience validating data across relational and NoSQL stores. Proven ability to design, implement, and scale automation frameworks in a collaborative, Agile environment. Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to articulate complex quality risks and solutions. A proactive mindset with the ability to work independently and manage competing priorities. Why Ryan? You’ll be part of a company where innovation meets real-world impact. We’re building something meaningful, and we want your expertise to help shape the future of our platform. Expect a collaborative environment, intelligent peers, and the opportunity to make technical and business decisions that matter.

title: Integration Testing Engineer
description: Job Information Date Opened 11/03/2026 Industry IT Services Job Type Full time Work Experience 5+ years City Hi tech city, Hyderabad State/Province Telangana Country India Zip/Postal Code 500081 Job Description Position Summary NetWeb Software is seeking an experienced Senior QA Engineer with strong expertise in integration testing, API validation, database testing, and automation testing. The role focuses on ensuring the quality and reliability of end-to-end integrations across enterprise applications, including Workato-based workflows and ChurnZero (CZ) integrations. The successful candidate will validate data flows, business rules, API interactions, and system behavior, working closely with development, product, and integration teams to identify issues and deliver reliable integration solutions. Key Responsibilities Integration Testing Design, prepare, execute, and maintain integration test plans, scenarios, and test cases. Validate end-to-end business workflows and data exchanges across multiple systems and applications. Verify data synchronization, completeness, accuracy, and consistency across integrated platforms. Identify, investigate, document, and track integration defects and data discrepancies through resolution. Collaborate with developers, product owners, and integration engineers to troubleshoot issues and validate fixes. Workato Platform Testing Test and validate Workato recipes, triggers, actions, mappings, connections, and workflow orchestration. Verify API requests and responses, payload transformations, business rules, and data handling within recipes. Validate error handling, retry mechanisms, exception paths, and recovery scenarios. Perform regression testing for recipe changes, enhancements, and newly implemented integrations. ChurnZero (CZ) Integration Testing Perform functional and integration testing of ChurnZero and connected enterprise applications. Validate customer data synchronization and the accuracy of customer-related records across systems. Verify health scores, customer journey events, usage data, and engagement workflows against defined requirements. Ensure business rules are correctly applied and data integrity is maintained across integration points. Data Flow & Database Validation Validate end-to-end data movement from source systems to target applications and databases. Write and execute SQL queries to verify data accuracy, completeness, consistency, and transformation results. Perform data reconciliation and investigate missing, duplicate, or inconsistent records. Analyze database records and integration logs to identify data quality issues and integration failures. API Testing & Performance Validation Design and execute functional, integration, and regression tests for REST APIs. Validate JSON payloads, request/response structures, authentication, authorization, status codes, and error handling. Use Postman and Swagger for API validation and documentation review. Execute API performance, load, and stress tests using JMeter, LoadRunner, k6, or similar tools. Analyze performance results, identify bottlenecks, and work with development teams to verify improvements. Automation & Quality Assurance Develop, maintain, and execute automated test scripts or integration test suites where appropriate. Identify opportunities to automate repeatable integration and regression scenarios. Participate in CI/CD quality gates and support test execution as part of build and deployment processes. Prepare test execution reports, defect records, test evidence, and root-cause analysis findings. Support UAT, production validation, and post-deployment testing activities. Collaboration & Continuous Improvement Work with cross-functional teams to understand integration requirements, acceptance criteria, and business outcomes. Participate in Agile ceremonies, test planning, reviews, and defect triage. Contribute to improving test coverage, test data practices, QA processes, and integration testing standards. Maintain clear documentation of test scenarios, results, dependencies, and known issues. Requirements Required Qualifications Experience & Education 5+ years of QA experience, with a strong focus on integration testing and enterprise application testing. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent professional experience may be considered. Hands-on experience testing Workato recipes and integrations is required. Experience testing ChurnZero (CZ) integrations and customer success workflows is required. Technical Skills Strong understanding of integration testing, end-to-end workflow validation, and data flow testing across enterprise applications. Hands-on API testing using Postman, Swagger, REST APIs, JSON, and related tools. Knowledge of API authentication and authorization mechanisms, including OAuth, request/response validation, and error handling. Strong SQL skills and experience with database testing, data validation, and reconciliation. Experience with API performance testing tools such as JMeter, LoadRunner, or k6. Understanding of regression testing, test design techniques, defect lifecycle management, and QA practices. Familiarity with test automation concepts, scripting, and CI/CD-based quality validation. Working knowledge of Agile/Scrum and tools such as Azure DevOps or Jira. Preferred Qualifications Experience testing integrations involving Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, or other CRM and enterprise applications. Knowledge of automation frameworks and scripting languages used for test automation. Exposure to cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure or AWS. Understanding of ETL/ELT concepts and enterprise data integration processes. Experience with DevOps practices, CI/CD pipelines, and automated deployments. Experience with production validation, integration monitoring, or support of business-critical interfaces. Preferred Candidate Profile Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and data accuracy. Able to independently plan and execute testing while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams. Clear verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues and test findings. Strong ownership of quality activities from test planning through execution, defect resolution, and production validation. Able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced Agile environment. Committed to continuous learning and improving integration and automation testing practices. Key Success Measures Comprehensive test coverage of Workato recipes, ChurnZero integrations, APIs, and end-to-end workflows. Early identification and clear reporting of integration defects, data discrepancies, and performance issues. Reliable validation of data accuracy and consistency across source and target systems. Effective regression and automation coverage for integration changes and releases. Timely support for UAT, deployments, and post-production validation with clear test evidence. Primary Skills Integration Testing | Workato Recipe Testing | ChurnZero (CZ) Integration Testing | API Testing (REST/JSON/OAuth) | SQL & Database Validation | Data Flow Testing | Postman | JMeter / LoadRunner

Automation and AI take the repeatable work so your manual effort goes where it adds the most value. You will work on applications that support ICE financial-markets infrastructure. A miss here is not cosmetic: defects can affect trading, clearing, data integrity, or regulatory evidence. We need someone who tests with that risk in mind. This is a hands-on Senior individual contributor role. You will influence design through code, reviews, and pairing. You will not manage people, and you will not be the sole owner of the organization-wide framework. Responsibilities Test automation Design, build, and maintain Playwright automation across UI, API, and integration layers. Use AI tooling to review requirements for ambiguities, missing edge cases, and untestable criteria before development begins. Generate test cases from requirements, then refine, consolidate, and prioritize them with engineering judgment. You own the final suite, not the model. Find coverage gaps, duplicate effort, and weak assertions in existing suites. Adopt and extend AI tooling where it pays off. Building custom agent skills or MCP servers is a plus, not the core of the job. Functional test ownership Own functional coverage and test strategy for assigned applications across UI, services, and integration points. Expect a mix of automation and exploratory work, weighted toward automation once a flow is stable. Perform manual, exploratory, and scenario-based testing where human judgment matters most. Triage, reproduce, and document defects, and drive them to resolution. Provide evidence-based release readiness to engineering and product leadership. Produce clear reporting on coverage, execution results, defect trends, and release risk. Technical influence Raise the quality of automation through code review and pairing with QA engineers. Partner with software engineers, product managers, and DevOps to move quality work earlier in the delivery cycle. title: Builder QA II
description: Job Description You are an engineer who specialises in proving things work. The distinction between “dev” and “QA” work is not one we maintain: you read the application code, you write production-grade Python, and you build agents. The difference is what you point them at. 1. Core DNA AI-Native Workflow. You use AI to accelerate everything you do as a default, not an experiment. You have opinions about which tools earn their place. Agentic Implementation. You build, debug and deploy autonomous agents — LLM-driven test generation, Playwright browser-use agents, self-healing locator strategies — against complex ERP screens and workflows. Legacy-to-Modern Bridge. Some of what you’ll test is a modern web rewrite. Some is a desktop application older than your career. Both are puzzles. Evidence Over Confidence. A generated test that has never been executed is not a test. You know your own false-positive and flake rates rather than claiming there aren’t any. 2. What You Own The ticket-to-test pipeline. An agent that reads a requirement or defect, understands the affected area, and produces a real test — grounded in the actual application, not in what the model imagines the application looks like. Hallucinated locators are the failure mode that kills these systems; preventing them is your problem. Execution and stabilization. Generation is the easy half. Your pipeline isn’t done when a test file exists or a ticket gets created — it’s done when the test has run against a real build, passed repeatedly, and earned its place in the suite. Flake is the enemy, because a suite nobody trusts is worse than no suite. Coverage that means something. You can tell the difference between a suite that covers the code and a suite that covers the risk. You use mutation testing and real defect history rather than counting tests, and you argue for the edge cases that actually bite: fiscal calendars, multi-currency, partial shipments, period-end adjustments. 3. Where You Might Lean In Test Generation & Grounding — the retrieval and context problem. How does an agent know what the screen really contains, what the business rule really is, and what changed in this release? Adversarial & Red-Team — you build agents whose job is to break things. Programmatic prompt optimization (DSPy), fuzzing business logic, hunting the input nobody thought of. Test Infrastructure & Agent-Ops — the factory the test agents run in: parallel execution, environment and data management, tracing, and the observability to know why a run went sideways. Legacy Surface Automation — desktop and thick-client applications where modern tooling doesn’t reach and the automation has to be built rather than installed. What You’ll Actually Do Build test-generation agents that take a ticket and produce an executable test grounded in the live application. Close the loop. Make generation, execution, stabilization and reporting one pipeline rather than four disconnected steps with a human carrying work between them. Automate the untestable. Wrap legacy business logic — the modules everyone has avoided because there’s no spec — in characterization tests that capture what the system actually does today. Kill flake. Find the root cause rather than adding a retry. Retries are how suites die. Red-team the financial logic. Build the agents that go looking for the case where the ledger doesn’t balance. Fix your own agents in production. Read the traces, find why it went sideways, make it not happen again. What Good Looks Like (Illustrative — real targets agreed with the hiring manager.) 30 days: Shipped your first agent-generated test into a running suite — generated, executed, stable. 90 days: Owning the ticket-to-test pipeline for a product area end to end, with a measured flake rate and a real coverage picture. 6 months: Other Builders reuse what you built. Escaped defects in your area are measurably down, and you can show why. The Stack Python, pytest, Playwright, SQL (Postgres/SQL Server), TypeScript, OpenAI/Anthropic, LangChain/LangGraph, DSPy, pgvector/Qdrant, Docker, CI/CD pipelines, OpenTelemetry, eval and tracing platforms (LangSmith / Langfuse / Braintrust or equivalent), desktop automation frameworks where the application demands it. And any other tool that helps us achieve greatness. Who You Are You’ve shipped one. You have built at least one autonomous agent or complex LLM workflow that real people used for real work — not a weekend demo. You know how it failed, because it did. You write real code. Python that goes to production and gets reviewed like anyone else’s. If your automation experience stops at a record-and-playback tool, this isn’t the role. The manual-task hater. You have a physical reaction to repetitive work. If you do it twice, you’ve already started drafting the automation. Technically fearless. A 500-table undocumented legacy schema isn’t complexity, it’s a puzzle about to get solved. You aren’t intimidated by spaghetti code — you’re the one who brings the sauce. Rigor over hype. You love the new models and you still ask for the numbers. You know the difference between a cool demo and a pipeline people rely on every release. Suspicious by instinct. Your first question about any green build is what it didn’t check. Why Join Us Quality is engineering here, not a stage gate. You are a Builder on the same ladder, with the same levels and the same expectations as everyone else in the squad. You build; you don’t sign off on other people’s work. The Final Boss of complexity. ERPs are the ultimate challenge for AI. If you can build agents that validate a General Ledger, you’ve solved the hardest version of this problem. Agentic autonomy. We don’t do tickets. We do missions. You’ll have real freedom over the models, frameworks and agent architectures you think will win. No red tape. If the agent works and the evals pass, we ship. No Change Management Committee — a “Does It Work?” policy. The Builder Tribe. You won’t be the only AI person in the room. You’ll be part of a small squad equally obsessed with moving faster, where your automation hacks are your biggest contribution rather than a hidden side project.
